title: Tokenframe compatibility maintenance and automation for fallback routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Maintain and automate the fallback model variant compatibility catalog ('Tokenframe' matrix) used by Smart Routing. The matrix captures tokenizer and context parity, KV-cache/rollout semantics, quantization/tooling compatibility, and runtime kernel expectations for each variant. This ticket scopes an audit pass, CI gating, telemetry gaps, remediation automation, and an operational runbook so routing policies can safely select fallback variants without introducing tokenization/context regressions.
goals: Audit tokenization parity for top-30 fallback variants against their primary counterparts
Define a canonical compatibility schema and store in a single source-of-truth (JSON + versioned manifest)
Add automated CI checks that block variant promotion when tokenizer/context semantics diverge
Create telemetry signals and dashboard for routing-induced failures and degraded outputs
Ship remediation automation that suggests nearest compatible variant or flags manual review
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility schema defined and approved by RTE and Applied ML
Automated parity test added to model-onboarding CI with unit tests and sample corpora
Routing layer reads manifest and enforces compatibility constraints during fallback selection
Dashboard surfaces parity regressions and per-customer fallback incidents
Runbook and escalation path documented with example commands and rollback steps
out_of_scope: Manual correction of historical variant mappings (handled by a separate cleanup epic)
Extending support to non-text modalities (vision/audio) in this iteration
plan: Week 1: Define compatibility schema (fields: tokenizer_id, tokenizer_version, max_context, kv_semantics, quant_profile, kernel_features, known_diffs)
Week 1-2: Run token-level roundtrip tests on representative prompt sets for top-30 variants
Week 2: Implement manifest storage in repo (models/compat-manifests/) and small API for routing queries
Week 3: Add CI gates to onboarding pipeline: fail if tokenizer_roundtrip_error_rate > threshold
Week 3-4: Instrument routing to log fallback decision and parity checks; build dashboard panels
Week 4: Implement auto-remediation suggestions and add runbook + pager playbook
risks: False positives in parity tests may block safe variants — need conservative thresholds
Large test corpora runtime could slow CI; will sample representative prompts and offline validation
Unexpected kernel-level differences in quantized variants that only appear at scale
Telemetry gaps may delay detection of subtle quality regressions during fallback
tasks: Create compatibility-schema.md and JSON schema in repo
Assemble representative prompt corpus (privacy-safe) and label expectations
Write token roundtrip harness that compares tokenizer outputs/token IDs across variants
Add manifest loader into routing service and unit tests for query paths
Add CI pipeline step and threshold config
Create Grafana panels and link to Incident runbook
Build automated remediation script that proposes nearest-compatible variant and opens a ticket when ambiguous
notes_and_decisions: Decision: prioritise tokenizer and context semantics over perf differences for compatibility gating
Decision: sample-based roundtrip tests will be used in CI; full-corpus nightly validation will run offline
Trade-off: allow fallbacks with minor tokenizer differences if divergence score < 0.02 for low-risk routes
Localization: variants with differing tokenizer vocab for non-en locales flagged as incompatible by default
